info.title: meka HTTP API
info.description: Service-to-service API for driving meka agent turns programmatically. Mirrors the wire format described in the HTTP API docs. A field that has no value is omitted from every response and event, never sent as `null`.

get.summary: `GET /v1/accounts`: every account, with whether a credential is stored under it.

post.summary: `POST /v1/accounts`: add an account, with its key when its backend takes one.
post.description:
A subscription backend's account is added without a credential and logged in through
`POST /v1/accounts/{name}/login`, as `meka account add` would have run the flow.

422.description: Invalid body: a name in use, an unknown backend, a setting the backend never reads, or a key where none is taken or none where one is; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

get.summary:
`GET /v1/accounts/{name}`: one account as the server serves it, with whether a credential is
stored under it.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /v1/accounts/{name}`: remove an account and the credential stored under its name,
or a credential alone when no account claims it.

404.description: No such account, and no credential under the name

422.description: A profile names the account; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

patch.summary: `PATCH /v1/accounts/{name}`: rename an account, moving its credential and every profile on it.
patch.description:
A rename is all an account takes: its other settings are what a login was made against, so
another endpoint or backend is another account.

200.description: The account under its new name

409.description: A session or sub-agent running on this server may run on the account, or another meka is refreshing its credential, which refreshes under its name

422.description: Invalid new name, or one in use; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

post.summary: `POST /v1/accounts/{name}/login`: store a credential for an account, replacing the one it has.
post.description:
An API-key backend takes the key in the body, as `meka account login` reads it from stdin, and
is answered 200 with the account. A subscription backend takes no body: the login runs in the
browser, and the answer is 202 with the URL to open and a `login_id` that
`POST /v1/accounts/{name}/login/{login_id}` completes with what the browser gave. A
`chatgpt-subscription` login also holds the loopback listener the browser is sent back to,
when the port is free, so a browser on this machine completes it on its own. Beginning a login
on an account that has one pending replaces it.

200.description: Logged in with the key; the account, now authenticated

202.description: A browser login begun; open the URL, then complete the login

422.description: No key for a backend that takes one, or one for a backend that logs in through the browser; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

502.description: The login produced no authorization URL in time; the reason is in the meka log

get.summary: `GET /v1/accounts/{name}/login/{login_id}`: where a browser login stands.

404.description: No such login pending on the account, or one that lapsed

post.summary:
`POST /v1/accounts/{name}/login/{login_id}`: complete a browser login with what the browser
gave, storing the credential.
post.description:
A login the loopback listener has already completed answers 200 as well; one it has already
failed answers 422 with why. A code the authorization server rejects ends the login, since the
code is spent; a paste that carries no code leaves it pending for another try.

200.description: Logged in; the account, now authenticated

404.description: No such login pending on the account, or one that lapsed

422.description: No code in what was pasted, another login's state, or an exchange the authorization server rejected; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

502.description: The token exchange got no answer meka can read, or the login lapsed; the reason is in the meka log

get.summary:
`GET /v1/config`: where the installation is, when `config.toml` was last read whole and
written, whether an edit awaits `POST /v1/config/reload`, and what only a restart applies.

200.description: Where the installation is and how this server stands against it

post.summary:
`POST /v1/config/reload`: read `config.toml` again and serve what a write over HTTP would
have: the accounts and profiles, the MCP servers brought to the file's entries, and the standing
instructions. Every other section is read at startup alone, and the answer names those that
changed.

200.description: What the reload applied, and what waits for a restart

422.description: `config.toml` fails to parse, or holds anything startup would refuse; nothing was applied

get.summary:
Liveness probe. Always returns 200 if the process is up and the listener is accepting; the
response handler running at all is sufficient proof. Used by Kubernetes / systemd to distinguish
"process crashed" from "process degraded".

200.description: Process is up and accepting connections

get.summary:
Readiness probe. Returns 200 iff the server is in a state where new turn requests can
reasonably be expected to succeed (session DB queryable, a profile configured, no *required* MCP
server stuck in `Failed`). Returns 503 with a body that names which subsystem is the blocker.

`GET /v1/info`: server identity and the permission surface. Authenticated; admits any token
holding at least one read scope (see [`crate::host::http::scope::ANY_READ_SCOPES`]). Tokens with
only write scopes get 403. The broad-read fallback is intentional: a token configured for
`sessions:r` to surface session listings can also see the server's own identity without
operators having to grant it anything else.
get.description: For which profiles exist and which one a session gets by default, see `GET /v1/profiles`.

get.summary: `GET /v1/instructions`: the standing instructions this server's agents run under.

put.summary:
`PUT /v1/instructions`: write the standing instructions to `instructions.md` in the config
directory, and run the sessions that open from now on under them.
put.description:
Refused when that file is not what this server reads: `--instructions`, `MEKA_INSTRUCTIONS`,
`MEKA_INSTRUCTIONS_FILE` or the `instructions/` directory stands above it, so a write would
change nothing a session sees, which is the one thing a write must not quietly do. Under
`config:w`, with the rest of the installation: the text is the persona every session runs
under.

200.description: Written; the instructions as this server now holds them

409.description: Another source is in charge of the instructions, so the file would change nothing; `detail` names it

422.description: Invalid body

get.summary:
`GET /v1/mcp`: configured MCP servers and their current connection state, and the names a
credential is stored under that no entry claims.

post.summary:
`POST /v1/mcp`: add a server to `config.toml` and to the running manager, which connects it
in the background.
post.description:
The answer's `state` is where the connection stands at once, `pending` for a server about to
connect; `GET /v1/mcp` says when it has. No login runs: a server whose endpoint asks for one
is logged in through `POST /v1/mcp/{name}/login`.

422.description: Invalid body: a name in use or reserved, keys that do not fit the transport, or a secret the entry cannot present; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

get.summary: `GET /v1/mcp/{name}`: one server's configuration and connection state.

200.description: The server as configured, with the kinds of credential stored for it and its connection state

delete.summary:
`DELETE /v1/mcp/{name}`: remove a server from `config.toml` and from the running manager,
closing its connection and dropping its tools from every session, and clear the credentials
stored under its name, the OAuth grant revoked at the provider once the removal is served,
where it can be. A name with credentials and no entry is cleared the same way.

404.description: No such server, and no credentials under the name

422.description: `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

patch.summary:
`PATCH /v1/mcp/{name}`: change a server's entry in place. A change to what its connection is
made from, or to a credential it stores, restarts it; a change to its tool policy alone applies
on the connection it holds; `disabled: true` stops it and `false` starts it.

200.description: The server as it now stands

422.description: Invalid body: keys that do not fit the transport, an `auth` block beside a stored bearer, or a secret the entry cannot present; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

post.summary:
`POST /v1/mcp/{name}/login`: store a credential for a server, or begin its OAuth login in the
browser.
post.description:
With `auth_token` or `client_secret`, the secret is stored, as `meka mcp login
--auth-token-stdin` or `--client-secret-stdin` stores it, and the server is restarted from its
entry; the answer is the server as it stands. With neither, the OAuth login `meka mcp
login` runs at a terminal begins: the answer is 202 with the URL to open and a `login_id`,
the server holds the loopback listener the browser is sent back to, and a browser elsewhere
is answered by posting the callback URL to `POST /v1/mcp/{name}/login/{login_id}`. The server
is restarted from the entry as the file then states it once the login completes. A
`client_credentials` server needs no browser: its login connects with the stored secret and is
answered 200 with the server, as a stored secret is.

200.description: The secret stored, or a login that needed no browser completed: a `client_credentials` server's; the server as it stands

202.description: A browser login begun; open the URL, then complete the login

422.description: A secret the entry cannot present, both secrets at once, or a login the entry cannot run: a stdio server, or one holding a bearer; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

502.description: The login did not begin: the server or its authorization server did not answer; the reason is in the meka log

get.summary: `GET /v1/mcp/{name}/login/{login_id}`: where a browser login stands.

404.description: No such login pending on the server, or one that lapsed

post.summary:
`POST /v1/mcp/{name}/login/{login_id}`: complete a browser login with the callback URL the
browser was sent to, when it could not reach the listener itself.
post.description:
A URL with no code in it is refused and leaves the login pending, as an account's is. The
answer waits for the exchange and the commit; the restart connects in the background, so the
server it carries is `pending` until it has.

200.description: Logged in; the server as it now stands

404.description: No such login pending on the server, or one that lapsed

422.description: No code in what was posted, another login's state, or a login that had already ended; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

502.description: The exchange at the authorization server failed; the reason is in the meka log

post.summary:
`POST /v1/mcp/{name}/logout`: clear every credential stored for a server and restart it
without them, the OAuth grant revoked at the provider once that is served, where it can be. A
server holding none is left as it is.

404.description: No such server, and no credentials under the name

422.description: `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

post.description:
An impatience button rather than the only route back: a server that failed its initial connect
is already being retried in the background with exponential backoff. This collapses the wait for
an operator who has just fixed whatever was wrong.

200.description: Read `state` for where the server now stands

422.description: Server is disabled in config

502.description: Re-establishing a connected server's transport did not finish in time

get.summary: `GET /v1/mcp/{name}/tools`: what one MCP server advertises, with resolved permissions.
get.description:
Queries the server live rather than reporting the registered set, matching `meka mcp tools`:
the point is to see everything it offers, including tools config is currently filtering out.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Words to search for. The memories the agent's own `memory_search` would find for them,
best first, each with the `snippet` it was found on; absent, the whole index.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
How many a search answers with at most. Default 10, clamped to 1..25. Ignored without
`q`.

parameters.name: referencing
parameters.description:
Only memories whose references name this: a memory name, path, URL or id, matched whole
and without regard to case.

parameters.name: unverified
parameters.description: Only memories not verified within this long, e.g. `90d`.

parameters.name: expired
parameters.description: Only memories whose expiry has passed.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description:
Only one tier: a project's memories, or the global tier for an empty value. Absent, every
tier.

200.description: Memory index, or the memories a search found

get.summary: `GET /v1/memory/{name}`: one memory, body included.

422.description: The name is in several projects and `project` named none
Invalid name, empty description, an unknown project, a name another tier holds, or an inline body the budget cannot take
Invalid name, or a name in several projects with none named

get.summary: `GET /v1/profiles`: configured profiles, with their account, backend and model only.
get.description:
Under any read scope, with the other discovery endpoints: a client that may run turns may see
which profiles it can run them on. No credentials are returned: they live in the database,
keyed by account name, and never transit this API.

post.summary: `POST /v1/profiles`: add a profile on a configured account.

422.description: Invalid body: a name in use, an account not configured, a setting the backend never sends, a profile that could not run, or `default: true` on a server started with `--profile`; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

get.summary: `GET /v1/profiles/{name}`: one profile, with every setting it states.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /v1/profiles/{name}`: remove a profile. The sessions recorded on it keep the name and
refuse to resume until it is configured again or they are moved.

422.description: Another profile names it in `fallbacks`; it is the default while two or more profiles would remain; or the server was started with `--profile` naming it; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

patch.summary: `PATCH /v1/profiles/{name}`: change a profile's settings, make it the default, or rename it.

200.description: The profile as it now stands

422.description: Invalid body: a value the key refuses, a setting the backend never sends, a profile that could not run on the result, `default: false`, `default: true` on a server started with `--profile`, a `name` sent beside other changes, or a rename of the profile the server was started with `--profile` naming; or `config.toml` holds something startup would refuse, which refuses every write until it is repaired

get.summary: `GET /v1/projects`: every project, with how many memories and sessions each holds.

post.description:
Under `memory:w`, with the rename and the removal: a project is a memory tier and nothing
else, so the scope that writes the tiers is the one that opens and closes them.

422.description: Invalid name, or one a project already has, exactly or under case folding

delete.summary: `DELETE /v1/projects/{name}`: remove a project nothing is on.

422.description: A memory or a session is still on the project; `detail` carries the counts

patch.summary: `PATCH /v1/projects/{name}`: rename a project, moving every session and memory on it.

200.description: The project under its new name

422.description: Invalid new name, or one another project has, exactly or under case folding

parameters.name: session
parameters.description:
Only the jobs planted on this session. A session with none, or an id no session has,
answers an empty list, as every listing filter does.

200.description: Scheduled jobs: every session's, or one session's with `session`

delete.description:
Keyed on the job id alone rather than nested under its session, because that is how a client
that read `GET /v1/schedule` holds it.

Takes the full id and 404s when nothing matches: a client holds the id whole from the listing,
and answering 204 to an id that matched nothing would report a still-firing job as canceled. A
gated job kept alive that way goes on running a shell command unattended.

get.summary:
GET /v1/sessions: paginated list. Returns persisted sessions from the DB (not just
in-memory entries) so audit consumers can see everything regardless of GC state.

parameters.name: include_children
parameters.description:
Include sub-agent sessions. Default `false`, which lists only root conversations.

Off by default because a dispatcher that spawns freely would otherwise bury its own
sessions under the sub-agents it started, and a client paging through the list wants the
conversations it created. Turn it on to audit what was spawned; `parent_id` on each row is
what reconnects a sub-agent to the session that dispatched it.

parameters.name: working_directory
parameters.description:
Only list sessions whose working directory is this one, compared in the canonical spelling
every session records.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Only sessions on this project; an empty value, the sessions on none.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description:
Only the sub-agents this session spawned, its direct children. A tree view expands one
node with one call and recurses for depth. Names sub-agents by definition, so
`include_children` is moot beside it; a session with none, or an id no session has, is an
empty page, as every listing filter answers.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Only the sessions on this profile.

parameters.name: pinned
parameters.description: Only pinned sessions (`true`) or only unpinned ones (`false`).

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description:
Only the sessions changed after this RFC 3339 instant, by the `updated_at` the record
shows: a turn or a change to what the session runs as, never a title or a pin.

422.description: The cursor is not one this server issued (`/errors/invalid-body`)

post.description:
Requires scope `sessions:w`. The created session's runtime (Agent, ToolRegistry,
HttpFrontend) is constructed eagerly so subsequent `POST /turn` doesn't pay the build cost.

422.description: Invalid body

post.summary: `POST /v1/sessions/import`: recreate a session tree from an export envelope.

422.description: Malformed or unsupported envelope

get.summary: GET /v1/sessions/search: the sessions whose conversations hold the words of `q`, best first.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
The words to search for. What was said is searched, not what tools were called with or
returned; a session whose title holds every word is listed first. Blank finds nothing.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many sessions to answer with at most. Default 20, clamped to 1..100.

parameters.name: include_children
parameters.description: Include sub-agent sessions. Default `false`, like the listing.

200.description: Matching sessions, best first, each with the words it was found by

get.summary: GET /v1/sessions/{id}: single session metadata.

delete.summary: DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}: drop the in-memory entry and (optionally) the DB row.

204.description: Session deleted (idempotent, also returned for unknown ids)

409.description: A turn is in flight; cancel first (`/errors/turn-in-flight`). Or another meka process holds the session (`/errors/session-locked`)

patch.summary:
PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}: update mutable session knobs (permission, approvals, cwd, profile) on
a live session without re-creating it. Returns the updated metadata.
patch.description:
Permission and cwd are hoisted on [`SessionEntry`] outside the runtime mutex precisely so the
PATCH handler can apply them without contending with a long-running turn; the change is
visible to the next agent operation that reads the cells.

409.description: A turn is in flight and the body names `cwd` or `profile`; cancel first (`/errors/turn-in-flight`). Or another meka process holds the session, so only that process may move it (`/errors/session-locked`)

422.description: Invalid body, or the id names a sub-agent's conversation, whose permission, cwd and profile come from the terms its parent spawned it with (`/errors/session-not-drivable`)

get.summary: `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/blobs/{hash}`: the bytes behind an image block, with their media type.
get.description:
Scoped to the session: the blob has to be referenced by one of this session's messages, so a
token that may read one session cannot walk every image in the store by hash.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: Content hash of an image block, as `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/messages` reports it

200.description: The image bytes, under their media type

404.description: No message of this session references such a blob

post.summary:
`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel`: interrupt the in-flight turn (if any) by firing the
session's cancellation token. Always returns 204 even if no turn is in flight (the
operation is idempotent and absence is observationally indistinguishable from a turn that
finished microseconds before the cancel arrived).

409.description: The named turn is not the one in flight
A turn is in flight; cancel first (`/errors/turn-in-flight`). Or another meka process holds the session (`/errors/session-locked`)

422.description: Invalid body, nothing to compact, or the id names a sub-agent's conversation (`/errors/session-not-drivable`), which no payload makes acceptable

502.description: The provider rejected or failed the summarizing turn. Read `type`: `/errors/provider-unavailable` is worth resending after a pause, `/errors/provider` covers everything meka does not classify, and `/errors/context-overflow` here means the conversation will not fit even to summarize it

503.description: An MCP server the checkpoint turn needed was unavailable (`/errors/mcp-unavailable`)

get.summary: `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/context`: live window occupancy plus cumulative usage.
`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/export`: the full conversation, including pre-compaction turns.
get.description:
Reads the raw event log rather than the materialized view, so turns that compaction hid from
the model are still in the export. That is the whole point of having it: `GET /messages` shows
what the model can see, and this shows what actually happened.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
`markdown` (default) or `json`. Markdown is a rendered transcript for a human; JSON is the
round-trippable envelope `POST /v1/sessions/import` accepts.

422.description: Unknown format

post.summary: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/fork: copy a session's conversation into a new one.
post.description:
Requires scope `sessions:w`. The copy starts with the source's full conversation and is
immediately usable; the source is left untouched and is not required to be in memory, so an
evicted session forks just as well as a live one. A source with a turn in flight is refused,
like every other write to it: the copy would end on a prompt nothing answered.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `ETag` of `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/messages` the copy was decided on. The fork is refused with 412 when the source has changed since.

409.description: A turn is in flight on the source; cancel first (`/errors/turn-in-flight`). Or another meka process holds the source (`/errors/session-locked`)

412.description: `If-Match` names a conversation that has since changed (`/errors/precondition-failed`); `revision` and `total` carry the current state

422.description: Invalid body, or the source is a sub-agent's conversation, whose copy is another sub-agent and so has no live session to hand back (`/errors/session-not-drivable`)

200.description: Items the model has not been shown, oldest first

202.description: Item recorded; the feed reports its delivery

422.description: Blank message, unknown class, or a sub-agent's session

204.description: Item withdrawn; it will not reach the model

404.description: No such item on this session, or already closed

409.description: The item is already in the conversation

200.description: Page of conversation messages. The `ETag` header identifies the whole conversation's current state, for `If-Match` on `POST /rewind` and `POST /fork`

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: Pending request id emitted by the matching `permission_required` or `elicitation_required` SSE event.

404.description: Session or request not found / already resolved

422.description: Invalid body, an answer of the other prompt's kind, `content` on anything but `accept`, an `accept` without `content` on a form or with it on a URL, or the id names a sub-agent's conversation (`/errors/session-not-drivable`), which no payload makes acceptable

post.summary: `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/rewind`: drop trailing turns from the conversation.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `ETag` of `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/messages` the edit was decided on. The rewind is refused with 412 when the conversation has changed since.

200.description: Turns removed. The `ETag` header is the conversation's new tag

409.description: A turn is in flight; cancel first (`/errors/turn-in-flight`). Or another meka process holds the session, as a running sub-agent's parent does (`/errors/session-locked`)

412.description: `If-Match` names a conversation that has since changed (`/errors/precondition-failed`); `revision` and `total` carry the current state

422.description: Invalid body, or fewer turns than requested

post.summary: `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/schedule`: plant a job on a session.

403.description: Insufficient scope, or a session that cannot do unattended work

404.description: Session not found, or scheduling is disabled on this server (`[schedule] enabled = false`), so there is nowhere for a job to go

422.description: Invalid schedule, or the session's job limit is reached, or the id names a sub-agent's conversation, which nothing outside its parent can fire a job on (`/errors/session-not-drivable`)

get.summary: `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/stream`: the session's feed, every event of every turn.
get.description:
Replays the events after `Last-Event-ID` from the feed's bounded ring, which spans turns, then
follows the live feed for as long as the connection is held. A client that rejoins after a turn
ended still learns how it ended from the replay.

The ring holds the latest `[serve] stream_replay_events` events within its byte budget, so a
client that was away longer than that is handed a `feed.gap` event saying its replay has a hole
rather than a transcript that silently skips.

A sub-agent's id names its own feed for as long as this process runs it: the same events a
session's feed carries, read-only, with `turn.started` naming the parent and its `agent_spawn`
call. Its prompts park on the parent's feed, so `attend` is refused here.

parameters.name: last_event_id
parameters.description:
Last event id the client received, for clients that cannot set a `Last-Event-ID` header
(browser `EventSource` sets it automatically; `fetch`-based clients often cannot).
The header wins when both are present.

parameters.name: attend
parameters.description:
Attend the session: show `permission_required` events and answer them. While an attending
reader is connected, a gated call on any turn parks for an answer instead of being refused
without asking. Needs `sessions:w`, the scope that answers.

409.description: Another meka process holds the session (`/errors/session-locked`), the token may only read and the session is not loaded (`/errors/session-not-loaded`), or the id names a sub-agent this process is not running (`/errors/subagent-not-running`)

422.description: `attend` on a sub-agent's feed, which is read-only (`/errors/session-not-drivable`)

get.summary: `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/tasks`: this session's background tasks, newest first.
`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/tools`: what this session's agent can call.
get.description:
Per-session rather than server-global because the catalog includes MCP tools and reflects that
registry's deferred / loaded state, neither of which is a process-wide fact.

409.description: Session is not loaded; run a turn first

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Stripe-style replay key. Same key + same body returns the cached response; same key + different body returns 409.

200.description: A held turn's response: the assembled turn (stream=false) or its live SSE stream (stream=true). The application/json schema applies only to the former.

202.description: A detached request's turn was admitted (detach=true, stream=false): the body is the turn record and `Location` names it under `/turns/{turn_id}`

409.description: A turn is already in flight (`/errors/turn-in-flight`), the Idempotency-Key was used with another body or is in flight on a concurrent request (`/errors/idempotency`), or another meka process holds the session (`/errors/session-locked`)

422.description: Invalid body, the id names a sub-agent's conversation, or the request still exceeds the profile's `max_request_bytes` after redaction. Read `type`: `/errors/invalid-body` is worth resending with a corrected payload, `/errors/request-too-large` with a smaller one or after `/compact`, `/errors/session-not-drivable` never is

429.description: Concurrency limit reached or idempotency-key cache full

502.description: The provider rejected or failed this turn. Read `type`: `/errors/provider-unavailable` was classified as transient and is worth resending after a pause, `/errors/provider` is the catch-all for everything else and usually needs the account or endpoint fixed, and `/errors/context-overflow` needs the conversation shortened first

503.description: An MCP server marked `required` was not connected, so the turn never reached the provider

get.summary: `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/turns`: every turn that began on the session, newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many turns at most. Default 50, clamped to 1..200.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The id of the oldest turn already read; the page holds the turns before it.

200.description: A page of turns, newest first

get.summary:

parameters.name: last_event_id

The last event id received, for a client whose transport cannot send the

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

200.description: Server-sent events: `session.created`, `session.updated`, `session.deleted`, the four turn lifecycle events and the two permission events, each naming its session

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Only the tasks in this status: `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `canceled` or
