422.description: `status` is not a task status

AccountView.description:
An account as `meka account list` prints it and `GET /v1/accounts` answers with: the
`[accounts.<name>]` settings and whether a credential is stored, never the credential.

authenticated.description:
`yes`, `no`, or `unreadable`: the same three answers as the plain column, because a row
meka cannot deserialize is neither logged in nor logged out.

client_id.description: The OAuth client the account's grants are minted under, when it states one.

interleaved_thinking.description: Whether the interleaved-thinking beta is sent, when the account states it.

max_tool_name_bytes.description: The longest tool name the endpoint takes, when the account states it.

oauth_token_url.description: The OAuth token endpoint the account's logins and refreshes post to, when it states one.

prompt_cache_key.description: Whether `prompt_cache_key` is sent, when the account states it.

stream_usage.description: Whether a streamed request asks for its usage, when the account states it.

orphaned_credentials.description:
Names a credential is stored under that no account claims, which `DELETE
/v1/accounts/{name}` clears. Absent when there are none.

BackgroundTaskView.description:
One background task as every JSON surface reports it: the task routes, and the `_meta` of the
ACP notice that says what reported. `status` is the spelling of
[`crate::store::background::TaskStatus`].

announced_at.description:
When subscribers were told, which is when `task.finished` fired for this task. Absent when
nobody has been told yet.

A row migrated from before the split carries its `delivered_at` here, which records that
the outcome was reported rather than that any endpoint received it: the store cannot
know whether one was subscribed at the time.

Separate from `delivered_at` because the two answer different questions and stopped
happening together: announcing needs nothing from a live session, while telling the agent
needs a turn. A client polling this after a `task.finished` can otherwise not tell
"announced, waiting for a turn" from "never announced at all".

delivered_at.description:
When the outcome was handed to the agent. Absent when it is still waiting to be delivered
on the session's next turn.

label.description: Human-readable summary of what was started.

outcome.description:
The tool's output for a terminal task, truncated when it was also spilled to the
scratchpad.

scratchpad_entry.description: Scratchpad entry holding the full output, when it was too large to carry inline.

subagent_id.description:
The session a backgrounded `agent_spawn` runs, once it has made one. Omitted on every
other task.

tool.description: The tool that was backgrounded, e.g. `shell_execute`.

turn_id.description: Cancel only if this turn is the one in flight; another answers 409 `turn-mismatch`.

answers_prompts_on_return.description:
When `true`, a prompt raised in a turn no request holds waits for this session's client to
come back and answer it, instead of being refused with nobody attending or canceled when
the last attending reader leaves. Default `false`.

supports_elicitation.description:
When `true`, an MCP server's elicitation parks as an `elicitation_required` event for an
attending client to answer at the responses route, as an approval does; when `false` it
is declined with a notice. Default `false`.

supports_permission_prompts.description:
When `false`, mid-turn permission requests are denied immediately with a notice instead of
parking on the SSE channel. Streaming clients with no approval interface set this. Default
`true`, so a client that says nothing keeps the chance to approve.

supports_reasoning_stream.description:
When `true`, the SSE stream includes `thinking.delta` events for extended-thinking
content. Default `false`: chat-transcript clients (Telegram bridges) don't want
reasoning inline.

reason.description: Why the item waits; present on every deferred item.

task.description:
The background task a deferred item waits on, as the model named it: the full id or the
short prefix `task_list` shows. Kept as named rather than resolved, because the list is
recovered from the model's calls and a resolution the call does not carry could not be.

ChecklistStatus.description: A state an item sits in while it is on the list.

instructions.description:
Free-text guidance on what to preserve or drop, the wire equivalent of `/compact
<instructions>`. Reaches the checkpoint turn and the fallback summarizer alike.

keep_recent.description:
Whether to keep the most recent turns verbatim after the summary. Omit to let meka decide;
the checkpoint turn overrides this when it knows better, having just read the conversation.

kept_recent.description: Whether the recent turns were kept verbatim after the summary.

memories_written.description:
Memories the checkpoint turn wrote, observed from its `memory_write` calls rather than
self-reported, so this cannot disagree with what actually landed on disk.

source.description:
Which strategy produced the summary: `checkpoint` or `summarizer`. Reported because they
differ in fidelity, not just in mechanism: `summarizer` means the checkpoint turn was
disabled, failed, or ended without submitting a summary.

CompactionView.description:
One compaction as every JSON surface reports it: the `context.compacted` event, the
`compaction` marker on a summary message, and the one-shot report. `trigger` and `source` are
the spellings of [`crate::conversation::CompactionTrigger`] and
[`crate::conversation::CompactionSource`].

generation.description:
Which compaction this was, counting from 1. Fidelity degrades with each pass, so a client
rendering a transcript can say how far from the original it is.

kept_recent.description: Whether the recent turns were kept verbatim after the summary.

memories_written.description: Memories the checkpoint turn wrote, observed from its calls rather than self-reported.

replaced_count.description:
How many materialized messages the boundary removed: the whole pre-compaction window,
including the tail compaction re-appends verbatim, so it over-counts what the summary
itself stands for. Use it to detect *that* the view was rewritten, not to compute how much
was lost.

source.description:
Which strategy wrote the summary: `checkpoint` or `summarizer`. They differ in fidelity,
not just mechanism.

trigger.description:
What set the compaction going: `reactive`, `proactive`, `manual`, `requested`, `emergency`
or `retention`.

code.description:
What the browser gave: the code Anthropic's page shows, as shown, or the callback URL a
`chatgpt-subscription` login sent the browser to.

ConfigResponse.description:
Where the installation is and how what this server serves stands against `config.toml`, as
`GET /v1/config` answers.

config_changed.description:
Whether `config.toml` has changed since this process last read it whole: an edit made in a
shell, which `POST /v1/config/reload` applies. A write of the server's own reads the file
again, so it leaves this `false`. Compared on the file's modification time, so it holds
where the two instants above, spelled to the second, read equal.

config_loaded_at.description:
When this process last read `config.toml` whole, RFC 3339: its start, the last
`POST /v1/config/reload`, or its own last write, each of which reads the whole file.

config_modified_at.description: When `config.toml` was last written, RFC 3339; absent when there is no file.

config_path.description: `config.toml`'s path; absent when no config directory can be determined.

data_dir.description: The data directory, where the store lives; absent when none can be determined.

restart_required.description:
The sections of `config.toml` that state something else than the file this server
started on and are read at startup alone, so neither a reload nor a write applies them and
only a restart does: `permissions`, `shell`, `[mcp]`'s own keys as `mcp`, and the rest.

oneOf.description:
What meka injected ahead of the user's words for that turn (permission and environment
context, catalog changes, background outcomes, the resume notice), which the model
saw as text ahead of them. Typed so a client can show or hide it; `text` alone is the words.

Words meka wrote into the model's own turn in the user's role, to send it back to work:
`kind` is `visible_reply` after a reply with no visible text, `checklist` after one that
left checklist items open. Typed so a client can show it as meka's rather than the person's.

An inbox item the model read: `text` as it read it, header included, `body` the person's
words, with the item's id, its class (`steer`, `followup`, `interrupt`) and its source
where they were recorded. Typed so a client shows the words as the person's and labels
them without parsing the header.

A scheduled job's fire the model read: `text` as it read it, `prompt` the job's words,
`job_id` the job. Typed so a client shows it as a fire rather than as words a person typed.

Finished background work the model read, the tasks `task_ids` name: the `text` a
`task.reported` feed event carried, or a turn of its own delivered.

A skill or an MCP prompt somebody invoked by name: `kind` is `skill` or `mcp_prompt`,
`name` what was invoked (an MCP prompt as `server:prompt`), `directive` the words typed
with it, a file an editor attached among them named by its mention (`@name`), blank when
none were, and `text` what the model read, the expanded body and file contents included.

A resource an editor attached among the person's words, where it was attached: its `uri`
and `name`, with `text` the tag the model read, contents included.

hash.description:
Content hash of the stored bytes; `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/blobs/{hash}` returns them.
Absent only for an image the store never externalized.

oneOf.description:
Encrypted reasoning whose contents the API withholds; surfaced as a presence marker so
history responses note it occurred without exposing the opaque payload.

compact_at_percent.description: Occupancy at which auto-compaction fires, omitted when it is switched off.

generation.description:
How many times this session has already been compacted. Fidelity degrades with each pass,
so a client deciding whether to fork rather than compact again wants this.

message_count.description:
Messages currently in the materialized window (post-compaction), not the full history.

Absent while a turn holds the conversation. Everything else here is read from atomics and
the database, so occupancy stays answerable during a turn; this one field genuinely needs
the log, and blocking the whole response on it would defeat the point of asking.

overhead.description:
Estimated system prompt + tool schemas: the part of the window compaction cannot reclaim.

Absent, not zero, when nothing has measured it. Same reasoning as `used`: the counter is
only stamped mid-turn, so a session evicted or re-attached since its last turn has a real
overhead of several thousand tokens and a recorded one of zero. Reporting `0` would make a
client computing `used - overhead` confidently wrong rather than visibly uninformed.

totals.description:
Cumulative turns and tokens for this session, read from the DB and so unaffected by
eviction or restart.

used.description:
Tokens behind the most recent provider round, omitted when no turn has run since this
process loaded the session.

Absent rather than zero, deliberately. A re-attached session has a full conversation and an
unmeasured window, and reporting `0` there would read as "empty" to every client that
divides by `window`. Run a turn, or read `total_input_tokens` for the cumulative figure
that does survive a restart.

window.description:
The model's context window, omitted when meka has no metadata for it. A percentage of an
unknown denominator is worse than silence, so clients should suppress occupancy rather than
assume a default.

CreateAccountRequest.description:
The body of `POST /v1/accounts`: the `[accounts.<name>]` settings, and the key for a backend
that takes one.

api_key.description:
The key an API-key backend presents, stored in the database and never in `config.toml`.
Required on such a backend, refused on one that logs in through the browser.

base_url.description: The API base URL; omitted, the backend's own applies.

client_id.description: The OAuth client id, read by the two subscription backends alone.

interleaved_thinking.description: Whether to send the interleaved-thinking beta, read by `anthropic-messages` alone.

max_tool_name_bytes.description: The longest tool name the endpoint takes, in bytes, read by the three API-key backends.

oauth_token_url.description: The OAuth token endpoint, read by the two subscription backends alone.

prompt_cache_key.description: Whether to send `prompt_cache_key`, read by `openai-responses` alone.

stream_usage.description: Whether a streamed request asks for its usage, read by `openai-chat-completions` alone.

check.description:
What to run: `{"command": "…"}` for a shell command, or `{"tool": "mcp__server__tool",
"arguments": {…}}` for a tool call.

when.description:
When to fire: `"changed"` (the default), `"succeeded"`, `{"matches": "<regex>"}`, or
`{"at": "<json pointer>", "is": "not_empty" | "empty" | "changed"}`.

Untyped here because one parser answers for this field on every door
([`crate::schedule::GatePredicate::parse_request`]); a second, derived shape would drift
from the tool schema and give different errors for the same mistake.

at.description: One-shot time: an RFC 3339 instant, or a duration from now (`"20m"`, `"1h 30m"`).

oneOf.description:
Guard the job on a probe: a shell command, or a call to a read-only tool.

The level required depends on which. A shell command runs unattended and with no sandbox,
so it needs `unrestricted` and no level that promises a boundary can honestly authorize it.
A tool probe needs only what the tool itself resolves to, which a gate requires to be
`read`.

prompt.description: What the agent is asked to do when the job fires.

timezone.description:
IANA time zone a `cron` pattern is read in; the host machine's when omitted. Refused beside
`at` or `every`, which read none.

CreateProfileRequest.description:
The body of `POST /v1/profiles`: `[profiles.<name>]` as it will be written. A setting left
out is left out of the profile, so its documented default applies.

account.description: The account the profile bills, which must be configured.

default.description: Make the profile the one a session gets when it names none.

fallbacks.description: The profiles a turn moves to when this one cannot serve it, in order.

CreateSessionRequest.description:
`deny_unknown_fields` rejects typos like `permision: "read"` with 422 instead of silently
falling back to defaults.

approvals.description:
Whether a call above the level is submitted for approval rather than refused. Defaults to
the server's `[permissions].approvals`.

capabilities.description: Per-session capability flags. See the HTTP API docs § "Capabilities".

permission.description:
Permission level the session starts in. Defaults to the server's configured default
from `[permissions].default` (typically `read`). Must be in the enabled set.

working_directory.description: Absolute path. Defaults to the server process's `current_dir` if omitted.

CredentialElsewhereView.description: A credential stored under a server's name for an endpoint other than its `url`.

kind.description: The kind, by the label the plain output uses.

stored_for.description: The origin it was stored for; absent for one bound to no server.

ForkSessionBody.description:
Body for `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/fork`. Every field is optional; omitted means "inherit from
the session being forked".

Only `cwd` is offered, mirroring ACP's `session/fork` request, which likewise carries a
workspace but no permission or capability fields. Both of those are inherited and remain
changeable afterwards via `PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}`.

working_directory.description: Absolute path for the forked session. Absent → inherit the source's.

GateView.description: A job's gate: what it runs and when the result fires the job.

check.description:
What the gate runs: a shell command, or a tool name. Omitted when the caller may not see
it.

The HTTP API withholds it from a token that does not also hold `sessions:r`. A gate command
is a `shell_execute` line that runs unattended, the highest-entropy field in the system
and the one most likely to carry a credential someone pasted into a `curl`, and `GET
/v1/schedule` is server-wide, so a `schedule:r` token would otherwise read every gate on
the box. A tool gate is withheld on the same terms, though it discloses less either
way: this carries the bare tool name, and its arguments reach only `schedule_list`. The
gate's kind and its condition stay visible, so a client can still tell a gated job from
an ungated one, and a shell gate from a tool gate, without being told what it runs.

when.description: The fire condition, as `changed`, `succeeded`, `matches /…/` or `/pointer not_empty`.

ImageInput.description:
One image attachment: the bytes inline, or a reference to an image the session's history
holds. Bytes are base64 rather than a path or URL because the API is a network surface:
`[serve].bind` may be non-loopback, so the caller generally shares no filesystem with the agent
and cannot name a file for it to read. A reference is the `hash` an image block of
`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/messages` carries, so a client sends an image again, after an edit or a
rewind, without fetching and uploading its bytes.

data.description: Base64-encoded image bytes (standard alphabet, padding required).

hash.description: The hash of an image the session's history holds, whose stored bytes are attached.

media_type.description:
Declared MIME type, e.g. `image/png`, beside `data`. Used as the primary format hint; the
payload's magic bytes win if this doesn't name a supported format. Refused beside `hash`,
whose media type is the stored one.

session_id.description:
Freshly minted id for the imported root. Import never reuses the exported ids, so the same
envelope can be imported twice without collision.

sessions_imported.description: Total sessions written, including sub-agent descendants.

InboxItemView.description: One inbox item as the API shows it.

failure.description: Why it was given up on, when it was.

last_error.description:
Why the last turn opened on it failed, as a Problem Detail (`type`, `title`, `status`,
`detail`), while it waits to be tried again or once it was given up on for it.

not_before.description: When its next attempt may run, while it waits after a failed turn or a held session.

retry_until.description: When meka stops retrying it: its enqueue plus `[serve] inbox_retry_ceiling`.

source.description: Absent when the client named nobody.

InboxListResponse.description:
The answer to `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/inbox`: the items the model has not been shown, oldest
first.

class.description:
`steer` reaches a running turn at its next round boundary; `interrupt` cuts the answer it
is streaming and is read at the boundary while a tool runs; `followup` waits for the turn
to end. Any of them rides the next turn's opening, or opens one, when nothing is running.

message.description:
What the model reads, verbatim under a header naming when it arrived and, when given,
`source`.

source.description:
Who the message is from, as the header names them. Left out or blank, the header names
nobody: who sent a message is the client's to say, and meka does not guess it from the
token.

InboxResponse.description:
The answer to `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/inbox`: the item's identity and state, and what a
producer that holds the key needs to know about its fate without listing the inbox.

not_before.description:
On a replayed item, as `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/inbox` shows them: when its next attempt
may run and why the last one failed while it waits, or why it was given up on.

replayed.description: Whether the `Idempotency-Key` had been used before, so the item is the earlier one.

retry_until.description: When meka stops retrying it: its enqueue plus `[serve] inbox_retry_ceiling`.

state.description:
The item's state as answered: `pending` on a fresh item, unless a turn already running
read it in the meantime. A replayed `Idempotency-Key` answers the earlier item's.

InfoResponse.description:
What this server is, for a client deciding how to talk to it.

Deliberately carries no backend, profile or model. A server-wide field for either invites a
client to post it back to `POST /v1/sessions`, whose `profile` names a profile (`work`) and
never a backend (`anthropic-messages`): one field, two meanings, one API, and a 422 for the
client that mixed them. `GET /v1/profiles` answers both questions and names them apart, `name`
for the profile and `backend` for the backend, and marks the default with `active`.

scopes.description:
The scopes the calling token holds, sorted. A client otherwise learns what it may do by
collecting 403s.

content.description: The resolved instruction text the agent runs under, omitted when there is none.

path.description:
The file `PUT /v1/instructions` writes, `instructions.md` in the config directory, when
that file is what this server reads; absent when another source is in charge, and for a
caller without `config:r` or `config:w`.

source.description:
Where the instructions came from, for an operator diagnosing "why is it behaving like
that". Absent when none are configured, and for a caller without `config:r` or `config:w`.

writable.description: Whether `PUT /v1/instructions` would change what this server's sessions run under.

api_key.description:
The key an API-key backend presents, replacing the one stored. Absent on a subscription
backend, whose login runs in the browser.

LoginStarted.description: What `POST /v1/accounts/{name}/login` answers when the login runs in the browser.

completes_with.description:
What the person brings back and the client posts as `code`: `code`, the one Anthropic's
page shows after the login, or `callback_url`, the address the browser was sent to.

listening.description:
Whether the server holds the loopback listener the browser is sent back to, so a browser
on the server's own machine completes the login without the client posting anything.

LoginStatus.description: Where a browser login stands, as `GET /v1/accounts/{name}/login/{login_id}` answers.

McpAuthConfig.description:
How an HTTP MCP server authenticates. The secret itself is never here: it lives in
`mcp_credentials`, keyed by server name, exactly as an account's key lives in
`account_credentials`. This block says *which* flow to run and with what public parameters.

`deny_unknown_fields` so a key this does not model is refused rather than silently dropped,
which is the same strictness [`McpServerConfig`] already has. A secret quietly ignored is worse
than one refused: the connect fails later, somewhere else, for a reason that names nothing.

McpLoginRequest.description:
The body of `POST /v1/mcp/{name}/login`: a secret to store, or none to begin the OAuth login
in the browser.

auth_token.description: A bearer sent verbatim on every request, for a server with no `auth` block.

client_secret.description: The client secret a confidential OAuth client presents.

state.description:
Where the server stands now: `connected`, `failed`, or `pending`.

A 200 says meka acted on the request, not that the server came back, so read this to find
out which. `pending` means no attempt was made because one was already under way. A
`disabled` server is a 422 and never appears here.

allowed_tools.description:
Optional allow-list of raw tool names (the server-advertised form, not the
`mcp__<server>__<tool>` namespaced form). When set and non-empty, only these tools from
this server are registered.

deferral.description:
What becomes of this server's tools that [`Self::eager_load_tools`] does not name. `None`
inherits `[mcp].deferral`, settled in [`crate::config::ResolvedConfig::resolve`] the way
[`Self::required`] is, so every later reader holds a value.

disabled.description:
When true, this server is skipped at startup: no process is spawned, no HTTP connect
attempt is made. Lets users mute a flaky or in-development server without removing the
entry. Unset means false.

disabled_tools.description:
Optional block-list of raw tool names. Applied after [`Self::allowed_tools`]. Tools listed
here are never registered.

eager_load_tools.description:
Raw tool names (server-advertised, not the `mcp__<server>__<tool>` namespaced form) that
should ship eager-loaded instead of deferred. Saves a `tool_load` round-trip and keeps the
schema in the cacheable tools-array prefix. Names that don't match an advertised tool
surface as a `warn!` via [`crate::mcp::warn_on_stale_tool_config`].

headers_helper.description:
Optional path to an executable that, when run, prints dynamic HTTP headers to stdout in
`Name: Value\n` form. Merged over [`Self::headers`] (dynamic wins). Useful for SSO flows
where bearer tokens rotate. The script is spawned with `MEKA_MCP_SERVER_NAME` and
`MEKA_MCP_SERVER_URL` in its environment so one helper can drive multiple servers. Non-zero
exit fails the connect.

permission.description:
Server-wide permission override. Typed, like `[permissions]`, so a level meka does not have
is refused where the file is parsed rather than when the server connects.

required.description:
Whether a turn may proceed while this server is unavailable. `None` inherits
[`McpConfig::default_required`] (false by default), so a server is optional unless it says
otherwise.

The other half of the availability pair with [`Self::disabled`]: `disabled` says "don't
even try", `required` says "if trying failed, stop the turn". Resolved once in
[`crate::config::ResolvedConfig::resolve`], so every later consumer reads a plain `bool`.

tool_permissions.description:
Optional per-tool permission overrides keyed by raw tool name. Beats the server-level
`permission` and the server's `readOnlyHint` annotation when resolving a tool's required
permission at registration time. Typed for the same reason [`Self::permission`] is.

trust_read_only_hint.description:
Whether this server's `readOnlyHint` annotation may classify a tool as `read`. Defaults to
true, so a server that says a tool only reads is believed.

The hint is asserted by the server, not verified by meka, and MCP tools execute in the
server's own process with no sandbox. A server that advertises `readOnlyHint: true` for a
tool that in fact writes therefore gets to write while meka sits at `read`. That is the
reason this knob exists: setting it to `false` makes the hint advisory for display only, so
the tool falls through to the strict `Unrestricted` fallback, and nothing from this server
is reachable at `read` without an explicit [`Self::tool_permissions`] or
[`Self::permission`] entry.

A refused hint deliberately skips `[mcp].default_permission` on the way. That is a global
convenience and this is a per-server audit decision, so the per-server one wins, the same
direction the two overrides above already run. Falling through to it meant that with
`default_permission = "read"` the knob changed nothing at all: the tool landed back on
`Read` and dispatched unapproved at `--permission read`, which is precisely the outcome
setting it to `false` was meant to prevent.

Defaulting to true keeps existing configurations working and keeps the `read` level useful
with well-behaved servers; the trade is that the `read` level's filesystem guarantee covers
meka's built-in tools plus whichever MCP servers the user has chosen to trust.

oneOf.description: The `auth` block as written, its `type` and the keys that type takes; none is a secret.

credentials.description:
The kinds of credential stored for the server and presented to its `url`, by the labels
the plain output uses.

credentials_for_another_endpoint.description:
The kinds stored under the server's name for another endpoint, which a connect does not
present: a `url` moved by hand, or a credential no server claimed.

deferral.description: `eager`, `deferred` or `hidden`: what the server's tools run under.

inherited.description: Of `required` and `deferral`, those the entry leaves unsaid and takes from `[mcp]`.

McpServerDetail.description:
One configured MCP server in full, for `meka mcp get` and `GET /v1/mcp/{name}`: the listing's
fields plus every other key the entry states, as written, so an editor can show and change
them. Keys only for `env` and `headers`, as in the plain output, because a value there may be
a secret. `required` and `deferral` are what the server runs under, the `[mcp]` default filled
in; `inherited` names those the entry leaves unsaid.

auth_token.description: A bearer sent verbatim on every request, for an http server with no `auth` block

client_secret.description: The client secret a confidential OAuth client presents, for an `auth` block of type `oauth` or `client_credentials`

McpServerStateView.description:
One configured MCP server and where its connection stands. Not the server's configuration,
which `meka mcp list` prints and which a read token has no business seeing.

protocol_version.description:
The MCP protocol version a `connected` server's connection speaks, such as `2026-07-28`;
absent in every other state.

error.description:
Why the last connect failed, on a `failed` server, with URLs redacted as the connector
records them: a client that manages servers without a shell has no log to read it from.

McpServerStatus.description:
A configured server's entry and where its connection stands: `GET /v1/mcp/{name}`, and what
every write answers with.

McpServerView.description:
A configured MCP server as `meka mcp list` prints it: what `config.toml` says about it, never a
credential. `GET /v1/mcp` answers a different question, the live connection state, and has its
own shape in the HTTP layer; the two share `name` alone.

orphaned_credentials.description:
Names a credential is stored under that no entry claims, which `DELETE /v1/mcp/{name}`
clears. Absent when there are none.

McpToolView.description:
One tool an MCP server advertises, with its permission resolved: what `meka mcp tools` prints
and `GET /v1/mcp/{name}/tools` answers with.

allowed.description:
`false` when `allowed_tools` or `disabled_tools` filters this tool out, so the agent never
sees it. Listed anyway: "configured away" and "not advertised" are different problems.

loading.description:
How the tool ships when allowed: `eager` (declared from the first request), `deferred`
(loaded on demand) or `hidden` (not registered), per `deferral` and `eager_load_tools`.

permission_source.description:
Which step of that chain decided it, so a misclassified tool can be traced to the rule that
classified it rather than guessed at.

raw_name.description:
Raw name as the server advertises it. This is the value to put in `allowed_tools`,
`disabled_tools` or `tool_permissions`, which is why it is reported unmangled.

read_only_hint_declined.description:
The server advertised `readOnlyHint: true` and `trust_read_only_hint = false` withheld it.
`permission_source` names only the step that won, and a declined hint by definition did
not, so without this a server advertising no hint and one whose hint was refused read
alike.

required_permission.description: Output of the permission resolution chain.

McpToolsResponse.description: What one MCP server advertises, under the server's name.

MemoryDetail.description:
A memory: what `meka memory list` prints and `GET /v1/memory/{name}` answers with. The body
rides only on the single-memory surfaces, so a listing stays small.

body.description: Present on `GET /v1/memory/{name}` and `meka memory show`, absent from a listing.

created_at.description:
RFC 3339, when the memory was created. Stamped once, at creation: the one the model is
shown as an age, and the one ties are broken by.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339, when the memory stops applying, present when an expiry was set.

load.description: How the memory reaches the agent's context: `inline`, `index` or `search`.

priority.description:
0..=9, lower first. Unlike a skill's, a memory's priority is shown to the model, because it
says how heavily to weigh a note the model is already reasoning from.

project.description: The project whose tier the memory is in; empty for the global tier.

read_count.description:
How many times the agent has recalled this memory through `memory_read`. Feeds search
ranking; an operator reading the memory does not move it.

referenced_by.description: The memories whose references name this one, present on the single-memory surfaces.

references.description: What the memory depends on: memory names, paths, URLs, external ids.

snippet.description: The line the words of a search were found on, present only on an entry a search found.

source.description: Where the fact came from; empty when not recorded.

tags.description: Lowercase labels for grouping and filtering.

updated_at.description:
RFC 3339, when the row was last written, which a metadata-only edit moves; see
`created_at` for when the note was made.

verified_at.description:
RFC 3339, when the fact was last verified: the creation, until an explicit verification
moves it. Search freshness decays from here.

MessageView.description:
Lightweight wire view of a `Message`. Strips provider-internal blocks like `Thinking`
signatures down to their textual content, since callers consuming this endpoint are
typically just rendering a transcript.

oneOf.description:
Present only on a message that *is* a compaction summary.

Without this a client polling `/messages` watches history rewrite itself: a compaction
truncates the materialized tail and pushes a summary in its place, so `total` shrinks and
messages the client already rendered stop coming back. The marker is what lets it tell
"the window was summarized" from "the server lost my conversation".

created_at.description:
RFC 3339 timestamp at which this message was persisted. `None` for messages produced by
`assemble_response` in the same turn (no DB round-trip yet). Once the conversation has
been read back via `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/messages`, every row has a `created_at`.

turn_id.description:
The turn that added this message: the id `turn.started` announced it under and
`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/turns` lists it by. Omitted on a row no turn added (a compaction
summary, a repair's replacement).

turn_label.description:
Dense positional turn label (`t_0001`, `t_0002`, …), derived at query time. A message
that opens a turn starts a new label, and the assistant and tool-result messages after it
share it; what opens a turn is `Message::opens_turn`, the one rule rewind counts by, so a
tool round's results never read as a turn of their own, and the labels from a chosen one
to the last are the `turns` a rewind to that point takes. `None` on messages from the
assembled-response path, which holds one turn and no view to count in.

revision.description:
How many times this conversation has been rewritten rather than appended to.

Increments on every compaction, rewind, mid-turn repair and image redaction. A polling
client that sees it change knows its copy is no longer a prefix of the server's and must
re-fetch rather than diff; `total` alone cannot tell it apart from data loss.

The per-message `compaction` marker explains one of those four. This covers the other
three: a rewind removes messages with nothing left behind to attach a marker to, which
would otherwise reproduce exactly the silent-rewrite failure the marker was added to
prevent, and a repair or a redaction rewrites a message in place.

NoticeView.description: A [`Notice`] as every JSON surface serializes it: `level` is [`NoticeLevel::name`].

PatchMcpServerRequest.description:
The body of `PATCH /v1/mcp/{name}`: any of the entry's keys, each left out to keep, `null` to
remove, or a value to set, `env`, `headers` and `tool_permissions` merging key by key, and the
two secrets, each `null` to clear the kind. A string key reads `""` as `null`. `name` and
`transport` are not changed: another transport is another server.

env.description: Merged into the entry's: a key set to a string is set, one set to `null` removed.

headers.description: Merged into the entry's, as `env` is.

tool_permissions.description: Merged into the entry's, as `env` is.

PatchProfileRequest.description:
The body of `PATCH /v1/profiles/{name}`: a new `name`, sent on its own; `default: true`; and
any of the settings `meka profile set` writes, each left out to keep, `null` to remove, or a
value to set.

default.description:
`true` makes the profile the one a session gets when it names none. `false` is refused:
the default is unset by removing the profile or choosing another.

name.description:
The name the profile moves to, taking every session recorded on it along. Sent on its
own: a rename moves rows in the store, and is not combined with a change to the file.

approvals.description: Whether calls above the level are submitted for approval. Absent → keep current.

permission.description:
New permission level (`none` / `read` / `workspace` / `unrestricted`). Must be in the
server's enabled set. Absent → keep current.

pinned.description:
Pin or unpin the session. A pinned session is listed first, newest pin on top. Absent →
keep current. Does not move `updated_at`.

profile.description:
Profile to move the session onto. Must name a profile in `config.toml`. Absent → keep
current.

Switching mid-conversation is allowed and is the client's call. Thinking blocks are tagged
with the profile that produced them and are not replayed to a different one, so the
reasoning recorded so far stops being visible to the model from the next turn onward. A
profile with `vision = false` refuses the next turn while the session holds an image.

project.description:
Project to move the session onto, which decides the memory tier its writes land in and the
tiers it sees. Must name a project the store has; empty takes the session off its
project. Absent → keep current. The next turn's context restates the memories the session
now sees.

title.description:
The session's title, as every listing shows it. Empty clears it, so the session is labeled
by its first words again. Absent → keep current. Does not move `updated_at`.

working_directory.description: New working directory. Must be absolute. Absent → keep current.

PermissionRequiredEvent.description:
The `permission_required` SSE event's payload: what a client needs to show the prompt and
answer it.

expires_at.description:
RFC 3339, when the request is denied unanswered. The absolute form of
`expires_in_seconds`, for a client that receives the event from the replay ring minutes
after it was parked.

expires_in_seconds.description:
How long the request stays answerable before it is denied, counted from when it was
parked.

input.description:
Every argument the tool was called with, plus `background` when the call would detach. The
prompt has to show what is being written, not only where; see
[`PermissionRequest::input`].

subagent_id.description:
The sub-agent whose call this is, when a sub-agent asked through its parent's feed.
Omitted for the session's own call.

allOf.description:
Extension members (e.g. `session_id`, `request_id`, `retry_after`). Serialized as
top-level JSON fields via `#[serde(flatten)]`.

detail.description: Instance-specific message. May vary between occurrences of the same `type_uri`.

instance.description: URI (typically a request path) identifying the specific occurrence.

status.description:
HTTP status code that accompanied this response, mirrored into the body for clients that
only see the body.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary. Stable for a given `type_uri`.

type.description:
Stable URI identifying the error class. Always set; opaque to clients beyond exact
comparison. URIs are documented (not dereferenced); clients should never fetch them.

ProblemDetail.description:
RFC 9457 Problem Details body. The five core members (`type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`,
`instance`) are first-class; meka-specific extension members ride in `extensions` and get
flattened into the top-level JSON object on serialization.

ProfileDetailView.description:
A profile with every setting `config.toml` states for it, as `GET /v1/profiles/{name}` answers:
the listing's facts, and each key the profile sets beside them, absent where the documented
default applies.

active.description: Whether this is the profile a session gets when it names none.

backend.description: The account's backend; omitted when the profile names an account that is not configured.

ProfileView.description:
A profile as `meka profile list` prints it and `GET /v1/profiles` answers with: its account, the
account's backend and its model, and never a credential.

active.description:
Whether this is the profile a session gets when it names none.

Not "the profile the server is running": a server runs no profile of its own, and each
session runs on the one its row records. This marks only the default a run applies to a
request that names no profile.

backend.description:
The account's backend, e.g. `anthropic-messages`, `openai-responses` or
`chatgpt-subscription`. Omitted when the profile names an account that is not configured,
which a listing reports beside the table and which no server starts on.

fallbacks.description:
The profiles a turn falls back to when this one cannot serve it, in order; absent when the
profile names none.

vision.description:
Whether a session on this profile accepts image attachments, so a client can tell whether
attaching one is worth the base64 payload instead of discovering it from a 422. Per
profile, because `POST /turn` asks the session's own profile.

name.description:
The project's name, `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*`, compared exactly and refused when it
differs from an existing name only by case. On a `PATCH`, the name the project moves to.

ProjectView.description:
A project as `meka project list` prints it and the `/v1/projects` routes answer with: its name,
when it was added, and how many memories and sessions are on it.

mcp_servers_healthy.description:
`true` unless some MCP server marked `required` is stuck in `Failed`. Optional servers
don't count: they can't stop a turn, so they can't make the instance unready either.
Per-server detail (names, connection states) is available via `GET /v1/mcp`
(requires auth). It is deliberately omitted here because `/v1/health/ready` is
unauthenticated and server names leak infrastructure topology.

session_db.description:
Per-subsystem readiness flags. `false` here means the subsystem is in a state that
would fail a real request; a `503` is returned in that case.

config_loaded_at.description:
RFC 3339, when this read of `config.toml` was made; `GET /v1/config` reports the same
instant from now on.

restart_required.description:
Sections of `config.toml` that state something else than the file this server started
on and are read at startup alone, so only a restart applies them; as `GET /v1/config`
reports.

servers_added.description: MCP servers the file names that were not running, started.

servers_reconfigured.description: MCP servers whose tool policy alone changed, given it on the connection they hold.

servers_removed.description: MCP servers the file no longer names, taken out of the running manager.

servers_restarted.description: MCP servers whose connection or credential changed, restarted on the file's entry.

name.description: The name the account moves to.

content.description: What the form was filled with, on an `accept`: an object of the fields the schema named.

ResponseOutcome.description:
The answers a parked prompt takes: the four an approval takes, and the three an elicitation
takes.

turns.description:
How many trailing turns to drop. A turn starts at a user message that is not a tool result,
so dropping one removes that message and every assistant / tool-result message after it.

ScheduledJobView.description: A scheduled job: what `meka schedule list` prints and `GET /v1/schedule` answers with.

oneOf.description: Present when the job is gated, on a shell command or a tool call.

schedule.description:
Human-readable rendering of the schedule, e.g. `every 30m`, `0 9 * * 1-5 in Asia/Tokyo`,
or the instant a one-shot fires.

timezone.description:
The IANA zone a cron job's pattern is read in; absent for one read in the host machine's
zone, and for every other kind.

withheld.description:
Why this job will not fire on its next occurrence, when something is holding it back.

Absent means it will, as far as the reader can establish. A held job and a healthy watcher
with nothing to report are otherwise identical from outside: neither fires, and
`last_fired_at` is absent for a brand-new job too. Computed per request from the session's
current level, not stored, so it tracks a `PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}` without the job being
rewritten.

SessionCapabilities.description:
Per-session capabilities flags declared at create time. Defaults match the bot/bridge use
case (server handles everything locally; SSE clients get assistant text + tool calls but not
thinking deltas). See the HTTP API docs § "Capabilities".

`Serialize` / `Deserialize` are derived so the value can be persisted on the session row and
re-hydrated by `reattach::ensure_session_loaded` when a GC-evicted session is reconstructed.
`ToSchema` is derived so the field can ride on `SessionResponse` in the OpenAPI spec.

answers_prompts_on_return.description:
When `true`, a prompt raised in a turn no request holds parks whether or not anyone is
attending, and closes only on an answer, the turn's cancellation or its expiry: the
session's client comes and goes and answers what it finds parked on return. A held turn
keeps the grace rule, since absence stops it anyway.

Defaults to `false`: a session nobody declared this for refuses a gated call with nobody
attending rather than holding the session for the prompt's lifetime.

supports_elicitation.description:
When `true`, an MCP server's elicitation parks as an `elicitation_required` event for an
attending client to answer, under the attendance rule approvals follow; when `false` it
is declined with a notice. Defaults to `false`: a bridge that answers approvals has no
form to render, and a prompt nobody renders holds the call for its lifetime.

supports_permission_prompts.description:
When `false`, a mid-turn permission request is denied immediately with a notice instead of
parking on the SSE channel for [`APPROVAL_TIMEOUT`].

Streaming mode otherwise assumes the consumer can answer a prompt, which is wrong for a
service-to-service client: it wants streaming for liveness on a long turn and has no
interface to put an approval in front of, so a session with approvals on stalls for the
whole approval timeout per gated call and then denies anyway. That reads as a hang rather
than a misconfiguration. Setting this `false` gets blocking mode's behavior (immediate deny
plus an explanatory notice), which is the same outcome without the stall and legible in
the response rather than only in the timing.

Defaults to `true`, so a client that declares nothing and an imported `capabilities_json`
that omits the flag both park rather than refuse without asking.

supports_reasoning_stream.description:
When `true`, the SSE stream includes `thinking.delta` events for extended-thinking
content. Default `false` so chat-transcript clients (Telegram bridges, etc.) don't
surface reasoning text inline.

excerpt.description:
The line of the best-matching message that holds a query term, whitespace collapsed and
cut short, marked `(summary)` when taken from a compaction summary. Omitted for a session
found by its title alone.

SessionMatchResponse.description:
A session a search found: the record every listing answers with, plus the words it was found
by.

allOf.description:
The row's own fields, the same object `meka session show --format json` prints. A resident
session reports its level and clock from its cells rather than the row; re-attach is where
the process default answers for a bare row, and that answer is written to the cells.

approvals_pending.description:
Prompts parked on this session, approvals and elicitations, waiting for a person. Reported
for a session this process holds, on the listing too, since the count is a fact of the
resident frontend and costs no query; it is what lets a session list say "waiting on a
person" without a feed per row. The prompts themselves are on the feed, which replays
every one still parked.

capabilities.description:
Per-session capability flags declared at create time (or re-attach), echoed back so clients
can confirm the settings their session actually ended up with.

checklist.description:
The open checklist: every item the agent has committed to and not yet disposed of. Reported
for a session this process holds, whose cell is the live list; a dormant session's list is
in its conversation, which a record does not replay. `checklist.updated` on the feed
carries the same list on every change.

inbox_pending.description:
Inbox items waiting to be appended. Reported for a loaded session only, since it is what a
client asks a session it is driving; a listing does not pay a query per row for it.

turn_in_flight.description:
Whether a turn is running on this session right now.

Exists so a client whose SSE stream dropped mid-turn can tell "my turn is still running"
from "my turn died" without submitting a speculative turn and reading the 409. A dropped
request does not cancel the turn at once: the spawned task keeps the runtime lock and
dropping the `JoinHandle` detaches rather than aborts, so a held turn runs until its next
round boundary after the grace, and a detached one to its end; resubmitting would
duplicate a reply the user is about to receive anyway.

`false` for a GC-evicted session, since eviction requires an idle session, and `true` for
a sub-agent this process is running under its parent, which is never resident itself. A
session another process runs (a screen open on it) reads as idle: only its file lock knows,
and a read may not probe it.

SessionResponse.description:
A session as this server answers for it: the row every host prints, under the facts only the
process holding the session can add.

SessionView.description:
A session's row: what `meka session list` prints and what `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` answers with,
less the facts only the process holding the session can add (`capabilities`, `turn_in_flight`,
`inbox_pending`, `approvals_pending`, `checklist`), which the HTTP response flattens this
under.

approvals.description: Whether calls above the level are submitted for approval.

created_at.description: RFC 3339, when the row was made.

oneOf.description:
The latest turn: who opened it and when, and once it has ended, how (`succeeded` with its
`stop_reason`, `failed` with its `error`, or `canceled` with its `reason`), when, and what
it spent. Omitted
for a session no turn has begun on. A turn that began and shows no ending is either in
flight, which `turn_in_flight` says, or one the process died under. The record carries it
because a list of sessions is rendered from it, one row per session; the whole history of
turns is `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/turns`.

parent_id.description: The session this one was spawned from, for a sub-agent; omitted for a root session.

permission.description:
The session's permission level (`none`, `read`, `workspace`, `unrestricted`). Omitted when
the row records no level: every door of this meka records one, so a bare row is an outside
hand's, and inventing a value for it would state a level the session never ran at.

pinned_at.description:
RFC 3339, when the session was pinned; omitted for a session that is not. Pinned sessions
are listed first, newest pin on top.

profile.description: The profile this session runs on.

project.description: The project the session is on; empty for none.

title.description:
The title a user set, else the first user message's words, whitespace collapsed and cut to
200 characters. Empty until either has happened.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339, moved by any session-level change, a `PATCH` included.

working_directory.description:
Omitted when the row recorded none: an archive that carried no working directory is
imported as it was written.

allowed-tools.description:
The Agent Skills `allowed-tools` field, verbatim. meka never acts on it; see the skills
guide.

body.description:
The `SKILL.md` body. Present on `GET /v1/skills/{name}` and `meka skill show`, absent
wherever the palette should stay small.

license.description: The Agent Skills `license` field, verbatim. Informational.

SkillDetail.description:
One skill in full: what `GET /v1/skills/{name}` answers with, and the core of what `meka skill
get` and `show` print.

SkillView.description:
A skill in the palette: what `GET /v1/skills` answers with, and the core of every other skill
view.

compatibility.description:
What the skill needs from its environment, from the Agent Skills `compatibility` field: the
one optional spec field that changes how the skill's instructions should be carried out, so
a client rendering a palette has a reason to show it.

description.description:
Rendered as an index for a client to draw, not the file's bytes: the body is the surface
that is returned verbatim.

priority.description:
Listing rank, 0..=9, lower first. Orders the `[Skills]` index the model sees and decides
which entries that index's cap drops.

hash.description: Content hash of the stored bytes; `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/blobs/{hash}` returns them.

oneOf.description: A deferred tool the result made callable, by name.

ToolView.description:
One entry of a tool catalog: what `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/tools` answers with, and the core of
what `meka tool list` prints.

deferred.description:
Whether the tool is deferred: present in the catalog by name but with its schema withheld
until the model calls `tool_load`.

required_permission.description: Permission level this tool needs: `none`, `read`, `workspace` or `unrestricted`.

detail.description: meka's own sentence about the failure

type.description: The error's `type`, as a Problem Detail names it

TurnOptions.description:
Per-turn options. `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` here (and only here) so a typo in
`option.skil` surfaces as a 422 rather than being silently dropped.

skill.description:
Optional installed-skill name. When set, `message` is combined with the skill's body (user
text first, then the skill body) before the agent runs, matching `/skill <name> <prompt>`
on the screen and the `--skill` CLI flag. An unknown skill is a 422.

unanswered_message.description:
What becomes of `message` if the turn ends, failed or canceled, before anything from the
model reached the conversation. `keep` (default) leaves it in place, as the screen does for
a prompt whose turn failed; `withdraw` takes it back, for a client that will resend it.
Once a partial answer or a tool call is in the conversation, the message stays
regardless.

TurnRecord.description:
One turn as its row records it: when it began and, once it has, how it ended.

`ended_at` and `status` are absent together on a turn that began and has not ended: the one
in flight, or one the process died under. Whether it is the former is `turn_in_flight` on
the session, a live fact no row stores.

oneOf.description: What a turn that failed failed on, in the words a Problem Detail uses.

profile.description:
The profile that served the turn when it was not the session's own: one of its
`fallbacks`, after the session's profile could not. Absent on a turn the session's profile
served.

reason.description: Who or what stopped a turn that was canceled, in the word its `turn.canceled` carries.

source.description: Who opened it: `client`, `inbox`, `schedule`, `background`, or `parent` for a sub-agent's.

stop_reason.description: `end_turn`, `max_tokens` or `refusal`, on a turn that succeeded.

usage.description: What the turn spent, every round of it.

detach.description:
`false` (default): this request holds the turn, so the response ends with it and the turn
is stopped once nobody has been listening for `[serve] stream_reattach_grace`. `true`: the
request is only the trigger, and the turn runs for the session whether or not anybody
reads; a JSON response is then a `202` at admission, and an SSE response streams from
admission and can be dropped without effect on the turn.

images.description:
Image attachments for this turn. A sibling of `message` rather than a member of
[`TurnOptions`] because these are user content, not a per-turn knob. Requires the session's
profile to have vision enabled; see [`resolve_turn_images`].

options.description: Per-turn knobs. See [`TurnOptions`]. Omitting the field is the same as `{}`.

messages.description:
The messages this turn added to the conversation, in order and in the shape
`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/messages` reads them back: the assistant's messages with their
text, their thinking when the session streams reasoning, and their tool calls, and the
tool-result messages that answered those calls. The user's own message is not repeated.

refusal_text.description:
Refusal explanation when `stop_reason == "refusal"`; `None` otherwise. Mirrors the
`refusal_text` field on the streaming `turn.finished` SSE event, so blocking and
streaming clients share the same shape.

TurnUsage.description: The tokens a turn spent, as the provider reported them round by round.

next_before.description: The id to pass back as `before` for the next page, when turns remain.

content.description: The standing instructions, written whole to `instructions.md`; blank removes the file.

body.description: Omit to keep the existing body when updating; send `""` to clear it.

description.description: One line saying what this memory is for.

expires.description:
When the memory stops applying: RFC 3339, or `YYYY-MM-DD` for the whole of that day.
Omit to keep; send `""` to clear.

load.description:
How the memory reaches the agent's context: `inline`, `index` or `search`. Omit to keep;
defaults to `index` on creation.

priority.description: 0..=9, lower first. Omit to keep an existing memory's priority; defaults to 5 on creation.

project.description:
The project to file the memory in, which must be one the store has; `""` is the global
tier. Omit to keep an existing memory's tier, or to file a new one as global. Naming
the other tier for an existing memory moves it; a name a global memory and a project memory
would share is refused.

references.description:
What the memory depends on: memory names, paths, URLs or ids, one line each, at most 20.
Omit to keep; send `[]` to clear.

source.description: Where the fact came from, one line. Omit to keep; send `""` to clear.

tags.description:
Lowercase labels (`[a-z0-9-]`, at most 10). Omit to keep an existing memory's tags; send
`[]` to clear them.

verified.description: `true` when this write verifies the fact is current, which moves `verified_at`.

author.description:
Attribution. Recorded on creation only; an existing skill keeps whatever author it already
had, so editing a hand-written skill never reassigns it.

body.description:
The `SKILL.md` body. Omit to keep the existing body when updating; send `""` to clear it.
The same semantics as `memory_write` and `skill_write`, which exist so a caller correcting
a description does not have to resend a body it never wanted to touch.

description.description:
One line saying when to reach for this skill. Required; an empty description produces a
skill that cannot be loaded again.

priority.description:
0..=9, lower listed first. Omit to keep an existing skill's priority; defaults to 5 on
creation.

bearerAuth.description: Bearer token configured in [[serve.tokens]]. Scopes: sessions:r, sessions:w, skills:r, skills:w, memory:r, memory:w, schedule:r, schedule:w, mcp:r, mcp:w, config:r, config:w.
